records.name: Grēta
records.facts_used: The catalogue refers Grēta to Margareta, within the Margareta/Margarita family that it traces to Latin margarīta, “pearl”. The 2006 English rendering manual independently lists Grēta among the Latvian renderings of Greta, which it marks as a diminutive of Margaret. Neither source gives the short form a separate meaning of its own. According to Laimute Balode and Renāte Siliņa-Piņķe’s 2025 article, Grēta was one of nine names added to the traditional Latvian name-day calendar in 2025. The catalogue separately reports a written record dated 1460. Neither date marks the creation of the name; the calendar addition is a recent official decision.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: The 1460 catalogue record is attributed, not independently inspected; the 2025 calendar addition is not a creation date. Checked location: Siliņš catalogue pp. 141; 229; Ahero PDF 100 / printed 103 Greta (dem. of Margaret) → … Grēta; LV-ALL93 PDF 3 (2025 calendar additions), visually checked. records.name: Rene
records.facts_used: Edgar Rajandi describes Rene as the French short form of Renatus, the brother name of Renata. He explains Renata from Latin as “reborn”. The Latin sense belongs to the older name family; it is not a trait of individual bearers. According to Rajandi’s 1966 book, Rene reached Estonia through literature only in the twentieth century and was especially frequent in Tallinn in 1962; earlier occurrences had been sporadic. This describes the historical spread he observed, not a first-use date or a current count.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: 1962 frequency is historical, not current. Checked location: Rajandi PDF 145 / printed 147, Renata and Renatus entries, visually checked. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.
